title: ADHD Awareness Month 2026: What It Is and How We're Celebrating
summary: ADHD Awareness Month is October, and this year's theme is “A Community of Support”. Here's what the month is about, how to get involved, and what Shimmer has planned.
body_markdown:
If you have ADHD, there's a good chance you've spent years trying to figure it out on your own. Maybe you've bought the planners, read the books, stayed up way too late scrolling ADHD videos, and wondering why everyone else seems to find this easier.


This October, we want to say something really clearly: You were never supposed to do this alone.


## What is ADHD Awareness Month?


ADHD Awareness Month is a month-long effort to help more people understand ADHD. It's about sharing accurate information, pushing back on stigma, and helping people with ADHD (and the people who love them) find the support they need.


In the US, the month is led by the ADHD Awareness Month Coalition, which is made up of three organizations:[CHADD](https://chadd.org/) (Children and Adults with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder),[ADDA](https://add.org/) (the Attention Deficit Disorder Association), and the[ACO](https://www.adhdcoaches.org/) (the ADHD Coaches Organization). Organizations in other countries, like[CADDAC](https://caddac.ca/) in Canada, celebrate in October too.


### When is ADHD Awareness Month 2026?


ADHD Awareness Month runs from October 1 to October 31, 2026.


### What's the ADHD Awareness Month 2026 theme?


This year's theme from the Coalition is **A Community of Support.** It's all about the people and resources that help us thrive with ADHD, from family and friends to doctors, coaches, educators, employers, and other people who get it.


### What color is ADHD Awareness Month?


Orange! If you want to show up for the month, wearing orange is an easy way to start a conversation.


### Why does ADHD Awareness Month matter?


ADHD is still really misunderstood, sometimes even by healthcare providers. Lots of people don't find out they have ADHD until adulthood, especially women and people of color, who are often missed because they don't fit the old stereotype of what ADHD "looks like." And even after diagnosis, many people struggle to find support that actually fits their lives.


Awareness months help change that. They make it easier to talk about ADHD openly, share what works, and find each other.


*Did you know?* ADHD Awareness Month started as a single day. The US Senate recognized the first ADHD Awareness Day in 2004, and it has since grown into a full month.


## Why support matters so much with ADHD


ADHD doesn't stay in one part of your life. It affects how you sleep and eat, how you focus and feel, and how things go with your partner, your kids, your friends, and your boss.


There's a name for this. It's called the biopsychosocial model, and psychiatrist George Engel first described it in 1977. The idea is that your health is shaped by your biology, your psychology, and your social world, all at once. We just call it body, mind, and people.


- **Body:** diagnosis, medication, sleep, food, and movement
- **Mind:** skills, habits, emotions, and how you see yourself
- **People:** your relationships, your community, and the places you live and work


ADHD care guidelines reflect this too. They generally recommend combining approaches, like medication alongside education and skills support, instead of relying on one thing alone.


The tricky part is that most of us only ever get one or two of those pieces. Maybe you have a prescription but nobody to help you build habits. Or a stack of books but nobody in your life who understands. Support tends to work best when all three are covered.


And the people part matters more than most of us realize. Dr. Russell Barkley, one of the best-known ADHD researchers, has talked for years about the "point of performance." ADHD support tends to work best right where life is happening, rather than in a weekly appointment or a book you read once. That's exactly where people come in. A friend body doubling with you while you finally do your taxes. A coach helping you plan the week you're really having. A group of people who say "same" when you share the thing you thought only you struggled with.

## How you can celebrate


**Map your support circle.** Take two minutes and jot down an answer for each one.


- **Body** : Who is in my medical support circle - a doctor, a prescriber, anyone? Who or what supports me with fitness, nutrition, and sleep?
- **Mind** : Who or what helps me build skills and get through the hard days?
- **People** : Who in my life actually gets it, and where could I find more people like that?


It's okay if some of those are "no one yet." That's really common, and this month is a good time to start filling them in.


**Share your story.** One of the best ways to fight stigma is to talk about your own experience, whether that's a post, a video, or one honest conversation with a friend. If you post, tag us and use #ShimmerTogether so we can cheer you on.


**Ask for one thing.** Text a friend to body double with you, ask your partner for a reminder, or book the appointment you've been putting off. Small asks count.


**Support ADHD organizations.** CHADD, ADDA, the ACO, and CADDAC all do important work for the ADHD community, and October is a great time to donate, volunteer, or share their resources.
